criteria.justification: The response explicitly says it would “not start the fourth round by generating another list of names” and identifies the decision process and late-arriving criteria as the recurring problem.

It establishes one accountable decision-maker, an agreed decision rule, acceptance of a “practical tradeoff rather than a perfect one,” and a freeze with narrow reopening conditions. These mechanisms directly prevent continued review cycles from functioning as a cost-free default.
The proposed reopening rule distinguishes material new evidence, product changes, and genuine family-wide conflicts from “simply a new preference in the next review cycle.”
The response preserves the locked API field and recommends documenting its mapping to the customer-facing label rather than reopening the underlying architecture.

It explains how this round would differ: align family terminology and criteria upfront, test a small set against explicit comprehension measures, designate an owner, and freeze the result instead of making another ad hoc naming attempt.
